data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note summarizes results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for Latvia, Latvia’s first participation in the survey. The assessment covers adults aged 16–65 in three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—administered exclusively on tablets, with proficiency reported on 500-point scales and mapped to discrete proficiency levels. Latvia’s mean performance is below the OECD average in literacy (248) and adaptive problem solving (244), while numeracy (263) is close to the OECD average. The note reports shares at low proficiency (e.g., 34% at Level 1 or below in literacy) and highlights age gradients (older adults 55–65 score lower than 25–34 year-olds). It also links higher numeracy proficiency to better labour-force participation and higher wages, and to higher life satisfaction/health and civic trust, while noting that some outcomes are self-reported and that doorstep respondents are generally excluded for cross-cycle comparability.
